what: how much of RiQuA can be scored as a character-attribution task

corpus.name: RiQuA
corpus.licence: none stated; fetched and converted locally, never committed

why_it_matters: addressee_confusion.py's 77.8% and its 205-v-4 separation rest entirely on PDNC - one annotation group, one scheme. RiQuA is an independent scheme with an addressee field, so it can test whether that finding is a property of attribution or of PDNC.
why_so_much_is_dropped: RiQuA's Speaker/Addressee relations point at MENTION SPANS and the corpus ships no coreference layer. 39.4% of speaker mentions and 35.6% of addressee mentions are bare pronouns, which cannot be scored against a roster of names. This is NOT a drop-in second copy of the PDNC task and must not be reported as one.
known_limitation: even within the kept rows, aliases are unresolved: 'Bob' and 'Bob Cratchit' are separate roster entries. A scorer must supply its own grouping or treat them as distinct.
next: run the arm and re-score with addressee_confusion.py; needs GPU
